output.summary: KEP-5758 proposes a per-container `ulimits` field in the Container SecurityContext, passed to runtimes through the CRI LinuxContainerSecurityContext. The KEP is at status implementable, stage alpha, and is limited to a small set of rlimits, with -1 (unlimited) allowed only under privileged Pod Security admission.
output.rationale: Users cannot set rlimits such as nofile, memlock, or nproc per container; they inherit runtime and host defaults, and workarounds lack portability and security. Reviewers pushed for narrower scope: the discussion led to supporting only a limited set of rlimits and dropping nproc in favor of the pids cgroup, since RLIMIT_NPROC is per real UID and can cross container boundaries. Privileged-only use of -1 was adopted because baseline/restricted could otherwise approximate unlimited values.

alternatives.option: Configure default ulimits in the container runtime
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says this applies a global default to all containers on a node, making mixed workloads with conflicting requirements impossible to support.

alternatives.option: Add an entrypoint script that adjusts ulimits
alternatives.why_not: The KEP calls this not secure, lacks reproducibility, and is very inconvenient to use.

The KEP lists it as a viable alternative, and reviewers noted it needs no privilege or runtime change; the KEP does not record a rejection rationale beyond the feature being proposed. Reviewers also raised it as an option (samuelkarp), so this is a documented alternative rather than a settled rejection.

alternatives.option: Support all rlimit types, aligned with docker and podman
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers asked to restrict the set; the author said the restriction was applied to support only a limited set of rlimits, with wider support deferred to beta or GA based on user feedback.

evidence.quote: Configure default ulimits directly in the container runtime - This applies a global default to all containers on a node, making it impossible to support mixed workloads
RLIMIT_NPROC limits the number of processes per real user ID, which means it crosses the boundary for containers (where userns UID remapping is not used).
I would suggest dropping support for this in favor of pids cgroup support that we have.
Only Pods with PSS in Privileged mode can use the ulimit feature
I have already added restrictions on the types of rlimit resources, supporting only a limited set of rlimits.
